sources.entry: Quick Caption - Transcribe and generate caption files (SRT, ASS and FCPXML) without manually entering time codes.

summary.one_liner: Quick Caption is a macOS app that transcribes video or audio clips while stamping timecodes automatically, then exports SRT, ASS, FCPXML, or TXT caption files.
keywords: final cut pro x import captions
use_cases: Creating subtitles for a video without manually entering time codes
Transcribing an interview or podcast clip into a text transcript
Producing SRT captions to upload alongside a video
Adding styled subtitles to a Final Cut Pro X project via round-trip XML
Generating ASS subtitles for playback in mpv or IINA or with ffmpeg
how_to_run: Download Quick Caption from the link in the README
Import a video (.mov, .mp4, .m4v, .mpg) or audio (.mp3, .m4a) file
Type each caption while the media plays; timing is recorded automatically
Adjust caption timing by dragging ends in the timeline and correct text in the Caption Editor
Customize fonts and colors in the Style Editor
Export as FCPXML, SRT, ASS, or TXT
notable: Automatically records start and end timestamps for each caption as you type, pausing and resuming playback
Exports to FCPXML for round-trip editing in Final Cut Pro X
Exports ASS files that carry the customized subtitle styling
Shows video framerate, duration, and name in the Style Editor
caveats: Only available for macOS as far as the README indicates
README does not describe automatic speech recognition; transcription appears to be typed manually while the media plays
No license or build instructions are given in the README
